title: Rivers and the Water Cycle (KS3 Geography)
subject: Geography
strapline: The drainage basin, the water cycle and river processes.
facts: The water (hydrological) cycle moves water between the sea, air and land: evaporation, condensation, precipitation and runoff.
A drainage basin is the area of land drained by a river and its tributaries.
The watershed is the boundary of high land separating one drainage basin from another.
Rivers erode the land by hydraulic action, abrasion, attrition and solution.
They transport material by traction, saltation, suspension and solution.
They deposit material when they slow down, building features like floodplains and meanders.
Typical landforms: waterfalls and V-shaped valleys in the upper course; meanders and floodplains in the lower course.
